sections.content:
12,470 people

were counted on the census as "tailors and dressmakers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Tailors and dressmakers prepare patterns and make, fit and alter tailored garments, dresses and other articles of clothing.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "tailors and dressmakers" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 45 to 49 years. Of the whole working population 11% were aged 45 to 49 years. For people working as "tailors and dressmakers", 12.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "tailors and dressmakers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "tailors and dressmakers" included:

  • security guards and related occupations
  • other skilled trades
  • artists

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "tailors and dressmakers" there were more women than men (66.4% compared with 33.6%).

This means "tailors and dressmakers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "textiles, printing and other skilled trades".

Men made up 33.6% and women made up 66.4% of "tailors and dressmakers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "tailors and dressmakers" included:

  • legal professionals (other)
  • public relations professionals
  • veterinarians

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "tailors and dressmakers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "tailors and dressmakers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "tailors and dressmakers", 10.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (51.3% compared with 48.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (53%) than self-employed (47%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leicester, this is in the region of the East Midlands.
